title: Repair Shadow Registry writer governance and measurement validity
objective: Repair the existing weekly Shadow Registry owner as one bounded integrity task: enforce the existing Shadow Sensor Registry schema rather than a reduced parallel validator; prevent placeholder evaluator strings or path presence from being classified as SCORABLE without a real evaluator contract/output; preserve immutable weekly evidence across same-week reruns; and stop the scheduled workflow from directly committing registry/governance-lane artifacts to main when the active Continuity + Learning governance requires registries to use the reviewed PR lane. Reuse existing owners and existing permitted automation/write patterns only. Do not create a new shadow registry, market rule, promotion path or write-policy semantic.
allowed_change_scope: tests/research/directly related Shadow Registry runtime, schema, evaluator-readiness, immutability and writer-governance tests

evidence.summary: Current governance allows scheduled direct main writes only in enumerated data lanes and explicitly classifies registries, schemas and specialist contracts as PR-required; direct-to-main changes in that lane are policy violations.
Current scheduled workflow runs on main, generates 04_MARKET_LEARNING/shadow_registry/LATEST.json plus weekly snapshots, commits them and pushes HEAD:main directly.

Existing owner schema requires definition provenance, version, input sources, horizon, output semantics, recoverability, forward-observation status, outcome horizons, canonical overlap and data-quality limitations for every sensor.
Current runtime registry omits most fields required by the existing Shadow Sensor Registry schema while using a separate reduced runtime contract.

Current validate_registry() checks only authority, sensor-id uniqueness, status and relevance_state. evaluate_sensor() marks any present-path sensor SCORABLE whenever evaluator is any non-sentinel string, and main() unconditionally overwrites weekly/YYYY-Www.json on a same-week rerun.

Current weekly output demonstrates the issue: BREADTH_FORWARD_FAMILY is classified SCORABLE with evaluator SOURCE_PRESENCE_AND_FUTURE_OUTCOME_REVIEW even though no validated evaluator output is bound in the runtime; summary reports scorable_count=2.

The original Shadow Registry activation PR contains unresolved Codex review findings matching all four reproduced current-main defects: writer governance, schema enforcement, false SCORABLE readiness and same-week immutability.

reproduction: On fresh main: (1) inspect 00_FMOS/CONTINUITY_LEARNING_ARCHITECTURE_v1.md governance lanes and confirm registries are PR-required; inspect .github/workflows/shadow-registry-weekly.yml and confirm it commits 04_MARKET_LEARNING/shadow_registry/LATEST.json plus weekly artifacts and pushes HEAD:main. (2) Compare each current REGISTRY.json sensor with SHADOW_SENSOR_REGISTRY_SCHEMA.json required_sensor_fields; confirm the runtime registry lacks required fields and validate_registry() does not enforce that schema. (3) Inspect evaluate_sensor(); confirm any evaluator other than None/NONE_RECOVERY_REQUIRED/RESEARCH_ARTIFACT_ONLY becomes SCORABLE when evidence paths exist. Confirm current LATEST.json marks BREADTH_FORWARD_FAMILY SCORABLE using SOURCE_PRESENCE_AND_FUTURE_OUTCOME_REVIEW without a validated evaluator output contract. (4) Run or fixture the generator twice for the same ISO week with different timestamps/evidence and confirm weekly/<week>.json is overwritten rather than preserved as immutable history. Stop as clean no-op for any sub-finding already fixed on fresh main, but retain the candidate while any reproduced defect remains.

positive: The existing SHADOW_SENSOR_REGISTRY_SCHEMA.json is actually loaded/enforced by the Shadow Registry validation path, and a fixture missing any required_sensor_fields fails closed; current registry rows are made compliant through existing owner semantics rather than by weakening the schema.

Calibration readiness can be SCORABLE only when the evaluator is an explicitly recognized existing evaluator with a validated output/contract required by the runtime; SOURCE_PRESENCE_AND_FUTURE_OUTCOME_REVIEW path presence alone cannot produce SCORABLE.

A same-ISO-week rerun cannot destroy or silently replace an existing immutable weekly evidence snapshot; LATEST may move, but durable historical observations remain separately addressable or the rerun fails/no-ops according to an existing owner pattern.

The scheduled Shadow Registry path no longer writes registry/governance-lane artifacts directly to main in violation of the active Continuity + Learning governance. Reuse an already permitted data lane or an existing reviewed branch/PR publication pattern; do not invent a new governance exception.

Because workflow files are in scope, execute the current repository-safety safepoint sequence before workflow modification, then run the Shadow Registry gate plus focused positive/negative tests and verify post-merge main readback.
negative: Do not modify, relax or delete SHADOW_SENSOR_REGISTRY_SCHEMA.json merely to make the current reduced runtime registry pass.
Do not treat file/directory existence, a non-empty evaluator label or legacy status as sufficient evidence of a working evaluator or scientific scorability.
Do not rewrite, delete or retrospectively relabel existing weekly snapshots or historical sensor evidence.
Do not create a second Shadow Registry, duplicate evaluator framework, new market threshold, market gate, model weight, promotion rule, canonical authority or portfolio action.
Do not broaden scheduled direct-main write authority or create a new write-policy semantic to preserve the current workflow shape; follow existing governance instead.
Do not change unrelated workflows, API budget, provider policy or market semantics.

forbidden_changes: relaxing the existing Shadow Sensor Registry schema
clean_noop_condition: A newer current-main owner has already repaired all reproduced writer-governance, schema-enforcement, evaluator-readiness and weekly-immutability defects without weakening authority, or the Shadow Registry has been explicitly retired/superseded by current governance.
stop_condition: Stop without code changes if the candidate hash/status/authority changes, fresh-state reproduction no longer confirms the defects, the Shadow Registry is intentionally superseded, or fixing the writer requires a new governance exception rather than reusing an existing permitted route.
escalation_condition: Escalate to FRAMEWORK_OWNER if remediation requires changing market gates, model weights, canonical authority, portfolio logic, API budget, new policy semantics, the scientific schema itself, or repository write-policy semantics rather than repairing the existing implementation to current owners.
